name: ktv_virtual_host_pipeline_v1
goal: Generate a fictional AI virtual female host inside a provided KTV scene image, then animate short commercial video shots.
primary_requirement: Do not use a real portrait cutout as the default route. The host must be an AI-generated fictional character.

required.name: scene_image
required.purpose: Venue/room reference that controls background, lighting, and spatial layout.

optional.name: character_style
optional.default: photorealistic elegant fictional KTV hostess, business reception style

optional.name: voiceover_audio
optional.purpose: Used only for talking-head or host outro shots.

stages.objective: Create and lock one fictional virtual host identity.
quality_gate: same face and hairstyle across references

stages.objective: Prepare the scene for stable character placement.
quality_gate: host placement does not block key venue details

stages.objective: Generate multiple identity-consistent keyframes of the virtual host inside the venue scene.
quality_gate: scene remains recognizable from source material

stages.objective: Generate short stable video clips from approved keyframes.
preferred_routes: WanAnimate for full-body controlled host motion
Wan I2V for subtle environment and approved keyframe motion
MuseTalk or AdvancedLivePortrait for close-up lip-sync shots
quality_gate: no major face swap or identity drift
motion is modest and commercially acceptable

stages.objective: Assemble clips into a reviewable commercial short video.
quality_gate: generated host shot passes manual review before upscale

known_gaps_to_close: Install or configure a stronger local identity-control stack for fictional character consistency.
Convert the local SDXL inpaint proof into a repeatable keyframe generation command.
Build a WanAnimate route that uses the approved virtual host keyframe instead of relying only on plain Wan I2V.
Add automated contact-sheet and quality-report generation per run.
